questions.stem: Sodium chloride has a high melting point (801°C). What is the best explanation for this?

options.text: The covalent bonds between Na and Cl are very strong
The strong electrostatic forces between many positive and negative ions in the lattice require a lot of energy to overcome
Sodium chloride molecules are very large
The metallic bonds in the structure are strong

questions.explanation: Ionic compounds like NaCl form a giant ionic lattice where each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions. The strong electrostatic attractions between many Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions throughout the lattice require a large amount of energy to break, resulting in a high melting point. NaCl does not contain molecules or metallic/covalent bonds.

questions.stem: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but it does when dissolved in water. Why?

options.text: Water molecules carry the charge
In solid NaCl the ions are fixed in position; when dissolved, the ions are free to move and carry charge
Dissolving creates new electrons that conduct electricity
The water breaks down NaCl into its elements

questions.explanation: In solid NaCl, the ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move to carry charge. When dissolved in water, the lattice breaks apart and the Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions become free to move throughout the solution. These mobile ions can carry electrical charge, allowing the solution to conduct electricity.

questions.stem: What is the structure of an ionic compound?

options.text: Simple molecules held together by weak forces
A giant lattice of alternating positive and negative ions
A giant lattice of atoms sharing electrons
Metal ions in a sea of delocalised electrons

questions.explanation: Ionic compounds form a giant ionic lattice, which is a regular three-dimensional arrangement of alternating positive and negative ions. Each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions, held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction in all directions. This is not a molecular structure.

questions.stem: Which of the following ionic compounds would you expect to have the highest melting point?

options.text: NaCl (Na⁺ and Cl⁻)
MgO (Mg²⁺ and O²⁻)
KBr (K⁺ and Br⁻)
LiF (Li⁺ and F⁻)

questions.explanation: MgO contains Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions, which have higher charges (2+ and 2-) than the ions in the other compounds (1+ and 1-). Higher ionic charges produce stronger electrostatic attractions in the lattice, requiring more energy to break. Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ are also relatively small ions, increasing the charge density further. MgO melts at about 2852°C.

options.text: Because the bonds between ions are weak
Because the ions are too far apart to hold together
Because a force can shift layers so like charges align, causing repulsion that shatters the lattice
Because ionic compounds contain no electrons

questions.explanation: When a force is applied to an ionic lattice, layers of ions can shift. This can cause ions with the same charge to be next to each other. The repulsion between like charges causes the lattice to shatter. This is why ionic crystals are hard but brittle - they crack along planes where like charges come together.
